verbs.name: edit.blend
verbs.description: Set an OVERLAY video track's LAYER blend mode — how the whole track composites onto everything below it (a standard layer blend mode). mode 'normal' (the default when omitted) = the usual alpha-over composite (clears the blend); other modes blend the layer with the base ONLY where the overlay has content: multiply (darken/burn), screen (brighten/glow), overlay (contrast), darken, lighten, difference, addition, subtract, softlight, hardlight. Useful for light leaks, textures, double-exposure, and grade layers. A LAYER property (it applies to the whole track) — put a clip on its own overlay track via edit.add_track to blend just that clip. VIDEO tracks only (the first non-empty video track is the base; empty tracks do not claim the base slot; audio/caption tracks ignore it). CPU-only → opts the timeline out of the GPU fast-track.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.name: edit.track_visible
verbs.description: Show or hide a visual timeline track without deleting clips or changing layer order. on:false hides a video or caption track consistently from live preview, exact frames, render, and export; on:true restores it. A hidden base video track leaves a black canvas behind visible overlays rather than promoting another track; hidden overlays and captions are skipped. Audio tracks are refused because audio uses edit.mute. Replay-safe: the flag lives on Track.visible and defaults true for old projects.

track.description: Video or caption track id to show/hide

on.description: true = visible in output, false = hidden from output

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.name: edit.track_lock
verbs.description: Lock or unlock a timeline track against accidental editing. on:true blocks timeline drag/trim/drop/delete/split/context edits and disables the selected clip's Layer drawer and Inspector controls while preserving selection, clips, audibility, visibility, and render output; on:false unlocks the track. Direct agent/API mutation remains explicit and is not silently blocked by this human-UI guard. Replay-safe: the flag lives on Track.locked and defaults false for old projects.

track.description: Track id to lock or unlock

on.description: true = locked against timeline edits, false = editable

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.name: edit.mute
verbs.description: NON-DESTRUCTIVELY mute or un-mute a whole AUDIO track. on:true silences the track in the audio mix; on:false un-mutes it. This is a FLAG on the track — the track's gain (edit.gain, dB) is NEVER touched, so a dialed-in level survives mute → unmute and survives a reload/reopen (this replaces an older mute that wrote -100 dB into the gain and lost the level when the session ended). A muted track contributes SILENCE to the mix; audibility is resolved at render/preview/export time by the rule: an audio track is audible iff it is NOT muted AND (no AUDIO track is soloed OR this track is soloed) — so an explicit mute always wins, even over solo. Video tracks contribute pixels only; imported video sound lives on its linked audio track. Video/caption targets are refused instead of storing a render no-op. Replay-safe: the flag lives in project state and the op is logged like any other edit.

on.description: true = mute (silence in the mix), false = un-mute

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.name: edit.solo
verbs.description: NON-DESTRUCTIVELY solo or un-solo an AUDIO track. on:true solos the track; on:false clears its solo. While any AUDIO track is soloed, only soloed audio tracks are audible in the mix and every other audio track contributes SILENCE — WITHOUT touching any track's gain (edit.gain). Like mute, this is a FLAG: the dialed-in levels are preserved and survive a reload. An explicit edit.mute still wins over solo (a muted track stays silent even if soloed). Video tracks contribute pixels only; imported video sound lives on its linked audio track. Video/caption targets are refused instead of storing a render no-op. Replay-safe: the flag lives in project state and the op is logged.

on.description: true = solo (only soloed tracks play), false = clear solo

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.name: edit.pan
verbs.description: Set an AUDIO track's NON-DESTRUCTIVE stereo PAN/balance (core editing): -1.0 = full left, 0 = center, +1.0 = full right. BALANCE semantics on the stereo track chain — center is unity (no filter emitted; untouched mixes stay byte-identical) and panning ATTENUATES the opposite channel on a cosine taper (never boosts, no clipping risk). Applied at the mix stage after concat/duck, so render, preview, and export.audio stems agree. Independent of gain_db (like edit.mute / edit.solo); survives reload. Video/caption tracks refused; out-of-range/NaN refused (not clamped).

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {old_pan, pan} on the track (OpEffect.track); one op appended

verbs.name: edit.paste_attributes
verbs.description: PASTE ATTRIBUTES: copy a SOURCE clip's attributes onto N target clips in one call. PURE ORCHESTRATOR (audio.cleanup_voice pattern): records NO op of its own — takes ONE auto-checkpoint, dispatches the existing replay-safe verbs (edit.grade/transform/crop/speed/gain/fade/effect/eq) per target, STOPS on the first failure and returns the checkpoint + revert_hint (never half-applied silently). Categories: grade (parametric+LUT) · transform (geometry+opacity, + crop when the source has one) · speed (1.0 copies as an explicit reset) · volume (gain dB for audio-track sources + fades when present; video gain is reported skipped because video tracks contribute pixels only) · effects (full effects list, SET semantics — an empty source list clears targets; + EQ when present). Attributes the source doesn't carry are listed in `skipped`, never silently dropped. The source clip itself is filtered out of to_clips. Kind mismatches fail through the sub-verb's own validation.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {status: ok|failed, from_clip, targets, which, applied[], skipped[], checkpoint, revert_hint}; sub-ops appended by the dispatched verbs

verbs.name: edit.slip
verbs.description: SLIP trim (core editing): shift a clip's SOURCE window by by_ms source-milliseconds (positive = show later content) — change WHAT plays without moving the clip. Timeline position, duration, fades, and keyframes untouched; downstream never moves. ONE op. Media clips only; speed ramps refused (clear, slip, re-ramp); bounds validated against the asset probe (no content before 0 / past the asset end); by_ms:0 refused.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip_id, slipped_ms, old_src: [in,out], src: [in,out]}; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.roll
verbs.description: ROLL trim (core editing): move the shared CUT between the two adjacent media clips whose boundary sits exactly at at_ms — the left clip's out-point and the right clip's in-point move together by by_ms timeline-milliseconds (positive = cut later). Total timeline length unchanged; downstream never moves. ONE op mutating both clips atomically. Constant speed honored (timeline delta x speed = source delta; exact at 1.0, +/-1ms rounding on retimed clips); speed ramps refused on either side; a crossfade AT the cut is refused (clear it first); emptying either clip refused; bounds validated against the asset probe.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {at_ms, rolled_ms, left: {clip_id, old_src, src_out_ms}, right: {clip_id, old_src, src_in_ms}}; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.slide_edit
verbs.description: SLIDE trim (core editing; named beside edit.split_edit — bare edit.slide is the slide-in/out ANIMATION verb): move a clip later/earlier between its two adjacent MEDIA neighbors, who absorb the move — the left neighbor's out-point and the right neighbor's in-point shift by by_ms timeline-milliseconds. The slid clip's own source window and duration are untouched; total timeline length unchanged. ONE op mutating both neighbors atomically. Needs a media clip on BOTH sides (use edit.move otherwise); speed ramps refused on all three; crossfades on a moving boundary refused; emptying a neighbor refused; bounds validated against the asset probe.
